platforms.name: Unconjugated PMO (naked phosphorodiamidate morpholino), incl. dual-ASO design
platforms.architecture: Charge-neutral PMO, 20-31mer, no ligand; uptake via dystrophic-membrane leak + fluid-phase endocytosis. Dual-targeting variant (brogidirsen) = two PMOs against two sites in the same exon, co-administered.
platforms.reaches_cell: Skeletal myofibers only at a low, highly variable level; diaphragm intermediate; cardiomyocytes essentially not reached at clinical doses (intact sarcolemma, no receptor route) - the key liability for a DMD55 program where LV function determines survival. Satellite cells poorly targeted by naked PMO.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes - nuclear splice switching is proven in humans for exons 44/45/51/53; activity is real but exposure-limited, not mechanism-limited.
platforms.human_pd: Best naked baseline = brogidirsen (exon 44, dual ASO): dystrophin 10.27% and 15.79% of normal in dose-escalation cohorts, rising to 16.63% (40 mg/kg) and 24.47% (80 mg/kg) of normal at 24 weeks. Single-ASO approved drugs: viltolarsen 5.7-5.9% of normal at wk25 (from 0.3-0.6% baseline); golodirsen 1.019% at wk48 (from 0.095%); casimersen 1.7% vs 0.8% placebo at wk48; eteplirsen 0.93% at 180 weeks.
platforms.dose_frequency: IV weekly, 30 mg/kg (eteplirsen/golodirsen/casimersen), 80 mg/kg (viltolarsen, brogidirsen up to 80 mg/kg). Weekly infusion for life.
platforms.toxicity: Best-characterised safety of any class. Brogidirsen: no SAEs, no discontinuations to 80 mg/kg/24 wk. Approved PMOs: hypersensitivity/infusion reactions, rare proteinuria/renal tubular signals at high mg/kg; no magnesium wasting.
platforms.access: Fully buildable internally - PMO chemistry is commoditised, CDMO capacity exists, and the regulatory path (dystrophin as accelerated-approval surrogate) is established. Fastest route to clinic for an ultra-rare exon 55 cohort; dual-ASO 'connected-sequence' design is in the literature and reproducible.

findings.claim: Brogidirsen dual-ASO exon 44 PMO gave dose-dependent dystrophin of 16.63% and 24.47% of normal at 40 and 80 mg/kg after 24 weeks, with no SAEs.
Viltolarsen raised dystrophin from 0.3-0.6% to 5.7-5.9% of normal at week 25; golodirsen 0.095% to 1.019% at week 48.
Casimersen: mean dystrophin 0.9% to 1.7% of normal at week 48 vs 0.5% to 0.8% on placebo.
Four PMOs are FDA-approved but efficacy is very limited, with delivery remaining the key obstacle (poor uptake, limited endosomal escape).

platforms.name: Anti-TfR1 Fab-PMO conjugate (Dyne FORCE; DYNE-251 / z-rostudirsen)
platforms.architecture: Humanised anti-transferrin-receptor-1 Fab covalently linked to exon-51 PMO; receptor-mediated endocytosis into TfR1-high muscle.
platforms.reaches_cell: Skeletal myofibers, diaphragm and heart. NHP: 5 weekly 30 mg/kg doses gave 43% (heart), 52% (diaphragm), 18% (quadriceps) exon 51 skipping at 8 weeks. mdx FORCE-M23D 30 mg/kg: 77% of WT dystrophin by Western in heart, diaphragm and quadriceps with near-complete sarcolemmal localisation in heart and diaphragm. Satellite-cell compartment: PMO delivered to satellite cells and found in nuclei of newly regenerated fibres 3 months post-dose (preclinical, platform-level).
platforms.functional_activity: Yes - human mRNA skipping, protein restoration, CK fall and functional endpoints moving in the same direction.
platforms.human_pd: DELIVER (exon 51): 20 mg/kg Q4W mean absolute dystrophin 3.71% of normal (muscle-content-adjusted 8.72%), >10x the 0.3% reported for eteplirsen; Registry Expansion Cohort met primary endpoint at muscle-adjusted 5.46% of normal at 6 months; sustained functional improvement to 12-18 months.
platforms.dose_frequency: IV 20 mg/kg every 4 weeks (registrational dose/regimen); 546 doses administered at that level.
platforms.toxicity: Favourable across 54 participants: no new treatment-related SAEs; IRRs 11%, all mild/moderate, no dosing stoppages; headache 16%, nasopharyngitis 16%, vomiting 14%. No anaemia, thrombocytopenia or kidney injury; no clinically meaningful electrolyte (incl. magnesium) changes - i.e. none of the PPMO liabilities.
platforms.access: Dyne is independent; BLA for z-rostudirsen submitted May 2026 seeking accelerated approval with priority review, launch targeted Q1 2027, Phase 3 FORZETTO running. Platform access only by partnership/licence; an exon 55 asset would be a new conjugate on their established Fab and tox package - plausible co-development but they control the IP and are prioritising their own exon franchise.

findings.claim: DYNE-251 20 mg/kg Q4W: mean absolute dystrophin 3.71% of normal, 8.72% muscle-content-adjusted; REC primary endpoint 5.46% muscle-adjusted at 6 months.
In NHPs, 5 weekly 30 mg/kg DYNE-251 doses produced 43%, 52% and 18% exon 51 skipping in heart, diaphragm and quadriceps at 8 weeks.
Safety across 54 DELIVER participants: all IRRs mild/moderate (11%), no treatment-related SAEs, no kidney injury or magnesium changes.
BLA for z-rostudirsen submitted May 2026 under accelerated approval; Phase 3 FORZETTO initiated.
TfR1-targeted FORCE conjugation enhanced exon skipping and prolonged dystrophin restoration in mdx mice.

platforms.name: Anti-TfR1 mAb-PMO conjugate (Avidity AOC; AOC 1044 / del-zota)
platforms.architecture: Full-length anti-TfR1 monoclonal antibody conjugated to exon-44 PMO (AOC). Longer circulating half-life than Fab format, supporting 6-weekly dosing.
platforms.reaches_cell: Highest measured human muscle PMO exposure of any class: ~200 nM PMO in skeletal muscle, up to 50x the concentrations reported for peptide-conjugated PMOs. Cardiac and smooth muscle targeted by design; preclinical atrial/ventricular exon 44 skipping ~7 skipped copies/ng cDNA. Human cardiac PD: none published.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes - skipping, protein and a biochemical disease-activity marker all move.
platforms.human_pd: EXPLORE44, 5 mg/kg: exon 44 skipping +37% absolute (7% to 44%, up to 66%); dystrophin +25% absolute over baseline (7% to 32% of normal; total dystrophin up to 54% of normal); CK reduced >80% from baseline to near-normal. n=10 in the 5 mg/kg cohort, 3 doses.
platforms.dose_frequency: IV 5 mg/kg every 6 weeks (10 mg/kg tested in healthy volunteers).
platforms.toxicity: Favourable; most TEAEs mild/moderate in DMD44 participants, well tolerated to 10 mg/kg in healthy volunteers. Note the AOC platform has carried serious safety events in other indications/payloads, so platform tox is payload- and dose-dependent, not a blanket clearance.
platforms.access: Hardest to access: Novartis completed the $12B Avidity acquisition on 27 Feb 2026; del-zota BLA accepted for priority review under accelerated approval (Sept 2026) with Phase 3 SAFARI44 as the confirmatory trial. An exon 55 program would compete for Novartis internal prioritisation; out-licensing the anti-TfR1 AOC format to a third party is unlikely. Treat as a benchmark and a validation of TfR1, not a realistic in-license.

findings.claim: AOC 1044 5 mg/kg: exon 44 skipping rose 37% (7% to 44%, up to 66%) and dystrophin rose 25% (7% to 32% of normal) with CK reduced >80%.
AOC 1044 achieved ~200 nM PMO in human skeletal muscle, up to 50x concentrations reported for peptide-conjugated PMOs.
Dosing was 3 doses once every 6 weeks in the 5 mg/kg DMD44 cohort; most TEAEs mild/moderate.
Novartis completed acquisition of Avidity on 27 February 2026 ($72/share, ~$12.0B), taking the muscle AOC platform in-house.
FDA accepted the del-zota BLA for priority review under accelerated approval; confirmatory Phase 3 SAFARI44 initiated.

platforms.name: Cell-penetrating peptide-PMO conjugates (PPMO: Sarepta SRP-5051; PepGen EDO)
platforms.architecture: Cationic/arginine-rich or proprietary 'enhanced delivery oligonucleotide' peptide covalently fused to PMO; adsorptive endocytosis.
platforms.reaches_cell: Reaches myofibre and (preclinically, e.g. Pip6a-PMO) cardiac muscle, but human exposure is roughly an order of magnitude below antibody conjugates.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes, skipping demonstrable in humans - but protein output did not follow at tolerated doses.
platforms.human_pd: PepGen PGN-EDO51 10 mg/kg: exon 51-skipped transcripts 4.26% but total dystrophin only 0.59% of normal - company concluded it could not dose high enough for meaningful benefit. SRP-5051 showed dystrophin increases but was discontinued.
platforms.dose_frequency: IV monthly (SRP-5051 30 mg/kg Q4W; PGN-EDO51 5-10 mg/kg Q4W).
platforms.toxicity: Class-defining failure mode: SRP-5051 caused hypomagnesaemia that was prolonged in some participants even after stopping, plus eGFR decline - development discontinued Nov 2024 on long-term safety/tolerability. PGN-EDO51 itself was well tolerated (all related AEs mild, no SAEs) but was stopped May 2025 for insufficient dystrophin; PepGen exited DMD entirely.
platforms.access: Available in principle (free IP space, several academic Pip/B-peptide series), but two independent clinical failures make it uninvestable for a new exon 55 asset. Deprioritise.

findings.claim: PGN-EDO51 10 mg/kg raised exon 51 skipping to 4.26% but total dystrophin only to 0.59% of normal; PepGen ended all DMD work.
Sarepta discontinued SRP-5051 after prolonged hypomagnesaemia and eGFR decline in some MOMENTUM participants.
Pip6a-PMO exon skipping activity in mdx skeletal and cardiac muscle cells is determined by cellular trafficking.

platforms.name: Endosomal Escape Vehicle (EEV)-conjugated PMO (Entrada ENTR-601-44)
platforms.architecture: Cyclic cell-penetrating peptide engineered for endosomal escape, conjugated to PMO; next-generation of the peptide class.
platforms.reaches_cell: Reaches skeletal muscle and gives measurable skipping in humans; no human cardiac PD.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes, but small in magnitude at the doses reported so far.
platforms.human_pd: ELEVATE-44-201 Cohort 1 (3 x 6 mg/kg IV, ~12 weeks): dystrophin +2.36% over a 4.00% baseline; exon 44 skipping +2.31% over 2.66%. An early functional (time-to-rise velocity) separation vs placebo was reported, ~3.5x MCID, on modest biomarker change.
platforms.dose_frequency: IV approximately every 4 weeks; dose escalation to 18 mg/kg planned in Cohort 3.
platforms.toxicity: Met primary safety objectives in Cohort 1. Program had been under FDA clinical hold, lifted 24 Feb 2025 allowing the adult MAD study; the hold history is a diligence item for the chemistry class.
platforms.access: Entrada is independent with exon 44/45/50/51 assets and no exon 55 program - the most realistic partner/licensor of a targeted-delivery chemistry for a new exon. But current human potency (2.4 percentage-point dystrophin gain) does not yet beat a naked dual-PMO, and higher-dose data are pending end-2026.

findings.claim: ENTR-601-44 Cohort 1 (three 6 mg/kg IV doses): dystrophin +2.36% over 4.00% baseline, exon 44 skipping +2.31% over 2.66%.
FDA removed the clinical hold on ENTR-601-44 on 24 Feb 2025, authorising a Phase 1b MAD study in adults.
Cohort 2 MAD and Cohort 1 open-label data expected by end-2026; Cohort 3 doses up to 18 mg/kg.

platforms.name: Vectorised antisense: AAV9-U7snRNA
platforms.architecture: Self-complementary AAV9 encoding modified U7 small nuclear RNA carrying the antisense sequence; one-time IV dose, continuous intranuclear antisense production.
platforms.reaches_cell: AAV9 tropism covers skeletal muscle, diaphragm and heart, and transduced myonuclei keep producing the antisense - the only class that addresses durability without chronic infusion. Does not transduce satellite cells durably, so dilution by regeneration remains.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes - efficient skipping and dystrophin restoration in mdx52 (exon 51) and exon 2 models; a 2026 paper extends U7snRNA to pseudoexon skipping with full-length DMD restoration in patient cells.
platforms.human_pd: Only human experience is the exon 2 duplication trial scAAV9.U7.ACCA (NCT04240314), systemic IV, results posted Sept 2025. No exon 55 or two-exon construct in humans. Preclinical dose-escalation has defined a therapeutic range for exon 2 skipping.
platforms.dose_frequency: Single IV dose; effectively non-redosable (capsid immunity).
platforms.toxicity: NHP GLP studies at clinically relevant doses showed no toxicity for AAV9.U7snRNA; however high-dose systemic AAV in DMD carries the known hepatic/complement/cardiac risk profile and pre-existing-antibody exclusion.
platforms.access: Academic origin (Nationwide Children's) - licensable, and attractive because a multi-cassette U7 vector can carry two antisense sequences, which is exactly what a frame-correcting 54-55 or 55-56 double skip needs. Build cost and CMC are much higher than an ASO; one-shot dosing with no titration is a real risk for a first-in-class exon.

findings.claim: scAAV9.U7.ACCA systemic IV trial for DMD exon 2 duplication posted results Sept 2025.
No toxicity in NHPs at clinically relevant doses of an AAV9.U7snRNA vector designed to induce DMD exon 2 skipping.
AAV9-U7snRNA gave long-term exon 51 skipping in mdx52 mice.
U7snRNA-mediated pseudoexon skipping restored full-length DMD expression in patient-derived cell lines (2026).

platforms.name: Integrin alpha-v-beta-6 peptide-ligand platform (Arrowhead TRiM) - adjacent, not yet an exon-skipping platform
platforms.architecture: Short peptide ligand binding avb6 integrin on myofibres plus lipid modifier; to date conjugated to siRNA (ARO-DUX4, ARO-DM1), not to splice-switching oligos.
platforms.reaches_cell: Skeletal muscle in humans (programs in clinic); deep durable knockdown in NHP skeletal muscle lasting at least 3 months after IV dosing. Cardiomyocyte targeting is a separate, still-preclinical Arrowhead tissue.
platforms.functional_activity: Demonstrated for RNAi payloads only. Splice-switching requires nuclear delivery of a steric-block oligo - not yet shown for this ligand, so it is architecture precedent, not efficacy precedent.
platforms.human_pd: none found for exon skipping with this ligand (searched Arrowhead TRiM muscle DMD exon skipping 2026).
platforms.dose_frequency: IV; NHP durability >=3 months supports quarterly-type intervals if it translates.
platforms.toxicity: Not established for an oligo-splice payload; no DMD human data.
platforms.access: Arrowhead partners selectively; this is a watch item, not a 2026-27 build option for exon 55.

findings.claim: Arrowhead's skeletal-muscle TRiM programs use a peptide ligand to avb6 integrin; IV dosing in NHP gave deep durable muscle knockdown lasting at least 3 months; cardiomyocyte targeting remains preclinical.

platforms.name: Exon-55-specific clinical precedent
platforms.functional_activity: Exon 55 appears in preclinical multi-exon 45-55 skipping work only: mutation-tailored PMO cocktails removing 3, 8 or 10 exons restored dystrophin in immortalised patient cells, and bodywide 45-55 skipping was achieved in mdx52 mice by systemic antisense. No published single- or dual-ASO optimised for a 54-55 or 55-56 frame-correcting double skip, and no evidence that one ASO drives coordinated skipping of two adjacent exons here - assume 2 ASOs.
platforms.human_pd: none found. Searches run: ClinicalTrials.gov DMD exon 55 (only hit: PBGENE-DMD ARCUS editing, NCT07429240); PubMed 'DMD exon 55 skipping antisense'; PubMed 'double exon skipping single ASO 54 55 56'; PubMed 'exon 55 PMO cocktail 54-55'.
platforms.access: Open field - no competitor asset to license or be blocked by; also no de-risking data. A nonsense mutation in exon 55 additionally means in-exon PTC removal has a second, non-skipping option space (readthrough/editing) worth a separate assessment.

findings.claim: Mutation-tailored PMO cocktails induced exons 45-55 skipping removing 3, 8 or 10 exons with dystrophin restoration in immortalised DMD patient cells.
Bodywide skipping of exons 45-55 was achieved in mdx52 mice by systemic antisense delivery.
A ClinicalTrials.gov search for DMD exon 55 returned no exon-skipping study; only Precision BioSciences' PBGENE-DMD ARCUS program (recruiting).

naked_baseline: Best unconjugated baseline is a dual-ASO naked PMO, not a single ASO: brogidirsen (two PMOs to one exon, exon 44), IV 40 and 80 mg/kg weekly, gave dystrophin 16.63% and 24.47% of normal at 24 weeks (dose-escalation cohorts 10.27% and 15.79%), no SAEs, no discontinuations. Single-ASO naked PMO ceiling: viltolarsen 80 mg/kg weekly = 5.7-5.9% of normal at week 25; golodirsen 30 mg/kg weekly = 1.019% at week 48; casimersen 30 mg/kg weekly = 1.7% vs 0.8% placebo at week 48; eteplirsen 30 mg/kg weekly = 0.93% at 180 weeks. All weekly IV, lifelong, with essentially no cardiomyocyte delivery - the baseline buys skeletal-muscle dystrophin only.
payload_vs_delivery: Delivery-driven: Dyne's 3.71-5.46% vs eteplirsen's 0.3-0.9% on the same exon 51 sequence target, and Avidity's ~200 nM muscle PMO vs peptide conjugates. Amenability-driven: exon 44's 4-7% pre-treatment dystrophin (natural skipping) inflates del-zota's 32% and ENTR-601-44's numbers. Potency-driven: brogidirsen's 24% comes from dual-site ASO design plus 80 mg/kg, not delivery. Exon 55 needs a two-exon skip - expect none of these magnitudes to transfer.
